title: Lead the AtlasOps production game day

bridge.knownConcept: Incident command, blast radius, recovery, and postmortem
bridge.applicationConcept: Application observability, environment drift, stale caches, authorization regression, rollback, and restore
bridge.analogyLimit: Application incidents include product, data, provider, and user-experience failures that infrastructure health alone may not reveal.

buildBrief: Prepare AtlasOps release checks, safe logs, health signals, backup and restore evidence, rollback instructions, ownership, privacy retention, and client handoff.
incidentBrief: A multi-fault scenario combines preview configuration drift, stale status data, a cross-tenant regression, and duplicate webhook delivery. Triage by impact, contain exposure, recover service, and write a blameless postmortem.

scenario.symptoms: Four signals appear together; one is a critical data boundary and the others affect freshness, delivery, and preview readiness.

acceptanceTests: Triage prioritizes authorization containment before lower-severity availability symptoms
Rollback and restore steps are executed against synthetic state with measured results
The postmortem separates trigger, contributing conditions, impact, detection, recovery, and prevention
evidence: Incident timeline and redacted signal captures
predictionQuestions: Which symptom creates the largest confidentiality blast radius?
Which actions contain harm before root cause is fully known?
defenseQuestions: Explain the triage order and evidence that changed it.
Distinguish rollback, restore, retry, and failover in this incident.
Identify one monitoring signal that would reduce detection time.
hints: Rank confidentiality, integrity, availability, and user impact before debugging convenience.
Contain the authorization path and preserve evidence before broad changes.
Build the timeline from observable facts and label every inference.
